title: St John the Baptist, Halifax
memorial_details: description: Originally described as an oak triptych, located in the South porch of the church, the memorial now presents as an elaborately decorated structure located in the area under the tower at the West end of the church. The lancet arched doors which carry the names are now firmly fixed in the centre of the structure, with the names fully visible. The names are under carved radiant crosses, with a Crown of Glory carved between the arches of the panels. That central section is enclosed by carved pilasters at the sides, carved rope work around the arch, with grotesques carved at the ends, and a carved shelf carrying the text 'These are they that came out of great tribulation'. This is now the only indication that this is a memorial, the central Dedication having been, presumably, closed in by the fixing of the doors across the central area of the triptych. A corniced, castellated pedestal runs across the top of the structure, with five roses carved on a frieze beneath, The areas to the sides of the arch below carry carvings, with a cherub beside the curve of the arch, roses at the sides, and the Greek letters Alpha and Omega below.
